summary.short: Dutch Act implementing the GDPR: names the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens as supervisory authority, sets national exceptions for special-category, criminal-offence and automated-decision processing, and provides for administrative fines. Applies to Dutch controllers and to non-EU controllers targeting persons in the Netherlands; articles take effect by royal decree.
summary.long: The Act supplements Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) in Dutch law. It establishes the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens (AP) as supervisory authority and sets its composition, powers and administrative fines, including fines up to 20,000,000 euro or 4% of worldwide annual turnover for certain breaches (Art. 6, 14, 17, 18, 21a). It sets national exceptions to the GDPR prohibition on processing special categories of personal data (Art. 22-30b) and rules on criminal-offence data (Art. 31-33), including for health care, insurers, employers, research and public-interest purposes. It permits automated individual decisions required by law or by a public-interest task, subject to safeguards (Art. 40), and restricts data-subject rights in listed cases (Art. 41). It sets rules for journalistic, academic, artistic and literary expression (Art. 43), research and statistics (Art. 44), archives (Art. 45), national identification numbers (Art. 46) and public registers (Art. 47). A legal representative's consent applies to persons under 16 (Art. 5). It contains transitional rules and requires an evaluation report within three years of entry into force (Art. 48, 50). Articles take effect on dates set by royal decree (Art. 53).
